transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m… mostly here because I can’t stop focusing on my face. Around my mouth and jaw, it looks droopy and uneven to me, especially in photos or reflections. People say it’s fine, but I don’t really see that. It feels obvious enough that I’ve been avoiding presentations and clients.
Is your concern about your face and jaw related to how you think it looks, or is it also about how it feels or functions?

It’s mostly how it looks. I don’t think my jaw isn’t working or anything… I just keep seeing this droop, like around my mouth and jaw, and it looks uneven to me in photos or reflections. Even when people say it’s fine, I can’t really believe them.
Has this concern about your face been causing you a lot of distress?

Yes. It’s… it’s been more than I want to admit. I canceled a major client presentation at the last minute because I couldn’t stand the thought of everyone looking at me. And I’ve been skipping networking things for an award, family gatherings too. My deadlines are starting to slip. It’s kind of… falling apart.
Does your perception of your face and jaw looking droopy and uneven stay the same all the time, or are there moments when it seems less noticeable to you?

It’s… mostly there all the time. Maybe some moments I try not to look, but if I catch myself in a reflection or a photo, I see the droop and unevenness right away. People can say it’s fine, but it still feels obvious to me.
Do you ever think that your face and jaw might actually look fine, even for a moment?

Maybe for a second, if I’m not really looking. But once I see a photo or catch my reflection, I just… I see the droop around my mouth and jaw right away. It feels too obvious, even when people tell me it’s fine.
Do you find yourself performing any repetitive behaviors, like checking your reflection, to try and reassure yourself about your appearance?

Yes… I do. More than I probably should.

Before work, or if there’s a family thing, I can get stuck in the bathroom mirror for a long time. I’ll take pictures on my phone from different angles, fix my makeup, adjust a scarf… then ask my husband if my face looks lopsided. Sometimes I look at photos of other women too, just to compare. It’s embarrassing.
Have you noticed any impact on your relationships with family or friends due to your concerns about your face?

Yes… it has. I don’t really like admitting that.

I’ve cancelled things I shouldn’t have, even a major client presentation at the last minute because I just couldn’t face being seen. And I’ve been avoiding networking events tied to an award… which is not good for work.

At home, too, family gatherings have started getting… strained. I miss things or I’m late, and then deadlines and plans kind of fall apart around me.
Are you finding it difficult to maintain your job or work responsibilities due to your concerns about your face?

Yes… it’s been hard.

I cancelled a big client presentation at the last minute because I just couldn’t stand the thought of being seen. And I’ve been skipping the networking things for that award, even though I know I shouldn’t.

Deadlines are starting to slip. It’s… affecting things more than I want to admit.
Do you think about your face and jaw at times when you're not looking in a mirror or seeing a photo of yourself?

Yes. It’s… kind of there even when I’m not looking.

I’ll be talking to someone or trying to work, and I’m still thinking about that droop around my mouth, or whether my jaw looks uneven. Even if people say I look fine, I don’t really believe it. It feels obvious.
Are there any areas of your life, besides work, where you feel like your concerns about your face are holding you back or causing problems?

Yes… family things, mostly. I’ve missed gatherings, or I show up late because I can’t get myself together enough to be seen.

It’s embarrassing. Plans kind of start to fall apart around it, and people get frustrated. I know it’s not just work anymore.
Are you avoiding social interactions or intimacy with your husband due to your concerns about your face?

Yes… I avoid things.

Not just with my husband, but… being around people in general has gotten hard. I’ve cancelled work things, missed networking events, and even family gatherings are starting to fall apart because I can’t face being seen. It’s affecting more than I want it to.
Do your thoughts about your face and jaw ever change, or are they always the same?

It changes a little, I guess… like sometimes it’s the droop near my mouth, other times it’s more the jaw looking uneven.

But it’s always some version of that. In photos, reflections… it just jumps out at me. Even if someone says I look fine, I don’t really take it in.
Are there any situations where you feel like your concerns about your face are completely overwhelming or dominating your thoughts and feelings?

Yes. It can take over pretty completely.

I’ll catch it in a photo or a reflection—the droop around my mouth, the jaw looking uneven—and then I can’t stop seeing it. Even if someone says I look fine, it just feels… obvious. It gets bad enough that I avoid presentations or meeting with clients.
Do you feel like your concerns about your face are affecting your relationship with your husband in any significant way?

Yes… I think it is.

I don’t really like talking about it, but it’s not just in my head anymore. I cancelled a major client presentation at the last minute, and I’ve been missing networking things tied to an award because I just can’t face being seen. My deadlines are slipping, and family gatherings… they’ve started falling apart too.

So yes, it affects him. It affects us.
Do you always focus on the same aspects of your face, like the droop and unevenness, or do your concerns shift to other features at times?

It’s mostly the same things… the droop and the unevenness around my mouth and jaw.

I notice it in photos or reflections, and then it’s just… there. I don’t really move on to other features much. It’s those areas that feel obvious, even when people tell me I look fine.
Do you worry that other people can see the flaws in your face that you notice?

Yes. I mean… I know people say they don’t, but it feels like they must.

The droop around my mouth, the unevenness in my jaw… once I see it in a photo or reflection, I can’t believe other people aren’t seeing it too. That’s part of why I’ve been avoiding presentations and clients.
Have you ever had a different concern about your appearance, not related to the droop or unevenness of your face?

Not really. It’s mostly this same thing… the droop, the unevenness around my mouth and jaw.

That’s what I keep seeing in photos and reflections. Even when people say I look fine, it feels obvious to me.
Do you think there's anything that could change your opinion about the droop and unevenness of your face?

I don’t know. People telling me I look fine hasn’t really changed it.

I still see the droop and the unevenness in photos or reflections, and it feels… obvious. Obvious enough that I’ve been avoiding presentations and clients. So I’m not sure what would make me believe it isn’t there.
Do you think others can tell that something is wrong with your face when they look at you?

Yes… I think so. I know people tell me they don’t see anything, but when I catch it in a photo or a reflection, the droop around my mouth and the unevenness in my jaw just look so obvious to me.

It feels like they must notice it too. That’s why I’ve started avoiding presentations and clients.
